concepts.name: Chemical Reaction
concepts.description: A process in which one or more substances undergo chemical change with bond reorganization to form new substances with distinct properties, characterized by change in state, colour, temperature, or gas evolution.
concepts.learning_objective: Identify the occurrence of a chemical reaction through observable experimental indicators.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: Whenever a chemical change occurs, we can say that a chemical reaction has taken place.
change in state, change in colour, evolution of a gas, change in temperature help us to determine whether a chemical reaction has taken place.

concepts.name: Chemical Equation
concepts.description: The symbolic representation of a chemical reaction using chemical formulas of reactants and products separated by a directional arrow pointing towards products.
concepts.learning_objective: Express chemical transformations in standard chemical equation format.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: A chemical equation represents a chemical reaction. If you recall formulae of magnesium, oxygen and magnesium oxide...

concepts.name: Word Equation
concepts.description: A preliminary textual representation of a chemical reaction stating the names of reactants on the left-hand side and names of products on the right-hand side.
concepts.learning_objective: Convert descriptive chemical observations into word equations.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: The word-equation for the above reaction would be – Magnesium + Oxygen -> Magnesium oxide

concepts.name: Skeletal Chemical Equation
concepts.description: An unbalanced chemical equation showing chemical formulas of reactants and products where the number of atoms of elements on LHS does not equal RHS.
concepts.learning_objective: Differentiate between skeletal equations and balanced equations.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: Such a chemical equation is a skeletal chemical equation for a reaction. Equation (1.2) is a skeletal chemical equation for the burning of magnesium in air.

concepts.name: Law of Conservation of Mass
concepts.description: Fundamental scientific law stating that mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction; the total mass of reactants must equal total mass of products.
concepts.learning_objective: Apply the conservation of mass principle as the governing rationale for equation balancing.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: Recall the law of conservation of mass that you studied in Class IX; mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

concepts.name: Balanced Chemical Equation
concepts.description: A chemical equation in which the total number of atoms of each element is identical on both sides of the reaction arrow, satisfying mass conservation.
concepts.learning_objective: Verify whether a given chemical equation satisfies atomic balance.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: the number of atoms of each element remains the same, before and after a chemical reaction. Hence, we need to balance a skeletal chemical equation.

concepts.name: Balancing Chemical Equations (Hit and Trial Method)
concepts.description: Systematic method of adjusting stoichiometric coefficients before formulas to equate atom counts on LHS and RHS without altering molecular subscripts.
concepts.learning_objective: Balance complex skeletal chemical equations using stoichiometric coefficients.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: This method of balancing chemical equations is called hit-and-trial method as we make trials to balance the equation by using the smallest whole number coefficient.

concepts.name: Physical State Notations in Equations
concepts.description: Indicating physical states of reactants and products using symbols (s) for solid, (l) for liquid, (g) for gas, and (aq) for aqueous solutions in chemical equations.
concepts.learning_objective: Annotate chemical equations with complete physical state and reaction condition symbols.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: The gaseous, liquid, aqueous and solid states of reactants and products are represented by the notations (g), (l), (aq) and (s), respectively.

concepts.name: Combination Reaction
concepts.description: A type of chemical reaction in which two or more elements or compounds combine to synthesize a single compound.
concepts.learning_objective: Recognize and write equations for combination reactions.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: Such a reaction in which a single product is formed from two or more reactants is known as a combination reaction.

concepts.name: Slaked Lime Formation and Whitewashing
concepts.description: Exothermic combination of quicklime (calcium oxide) with water forming slaked lime (calcium hydroxide), followed by slow reaction with atmospheric CO2 to form shiny calcium carbonate.
concepts.learning_objective: Explain the chemistry of whitewashing using CaO, Ca(OH)2, and CaCO3 reactions.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: Calcium oxide reacts vigorously with water to produce slaked lime (calcium hydroxide) releasing a large amount of heat.

concepts.name: Exothermic Reaction
concepts.description: Chemical reactions accompanied by the evolution or release of thermal energy into the surroundings, resulting in temperature rise.
concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish exothermic reactions from endothermic reactions on energetic criteria.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: Reactions in which heat is released along with the formation of products are called exothermic chemical reactions.

concepts.name: Respiration as an Exothermic Process
concepts.description: Biological oxidation of glucose in body cells releasing energy necessary for life maintenance, making cellular respiration an exothermic process.
concepts.learning_objective: Write the chemical equation for cellular respiration and justify its exothermic nature.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: Respiration is an exothermic process. C6H12O6(aq) + 6O2(aq) -> 6CO2(aq) + 6H2O(l) + energy

concepts.name: Decomposition Reaction
concepts.description: A chemical reaction in which a single reactant breaks down upon energy input to yield two or more simpler products.
concepts.learning_objective: Identify decomposition reactions and write balanced chemical equations for their pathways.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: In this reaction you can observe that a single reactant breaks down to give simpler products. This is a decomposition reaction.

concepts.name: Thermal Decomposition
concepts.description: Decomposition reaction triggered by thermal energy (heating), exemplified by heating ferrous sulphate crystals, limestone (CaCO3), and lead nitrate.
concepts.learning_objective: Predict products and observations (colour change, gases evolved) during thermal decomposition.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: When a decomposition reaction is carried out by heating, it is called thermal decomposition.

concepts.name: Electrolytic Decomposition (Electrolysis)
concepts.description: Decomposition of chemical compounds induced by passing an electric current, notably the electrolysis of acidified water producing hydrogen and oxygen in a 2:1 volume ratio.
concepts.learning_objective: Explain the electrolysis of water and justify the 2:1 gas volume ratio at cathode and anode.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: Activity 1.7 (Electrolysis of water) ... Is the volume of gas collected the same in both the test tubes?

concepts.name: Photolytic Decomposition (Photolysis)
concepts.description: Decomposition reaction initiated by absorption of light photons, exemplified by silver chloride and silver bromide turning grey in sunlight; historically utilized in black-and-white photography.
concepts.learning_objective: Describe photolysis of silver halides and its historical application in photography.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: White silver chloride turns grey in sunlight. This is due to the decomposition of silver chloride into silver and chlorine by light. 2AgCl(s) -> 2Ag(s) + Cl2(g)

concepts.name: Endothermic Reaction
concepts.description: Chemical reactions requiring continuous absorption of energy in the form of heat, light, or electricity to rupture reactant bonds and proceed.
concepts.learning_objective: Classify chemical transformations as endothermic based on enthalpy absorption.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: Reactions in which energy is absorbed are known as endothermic reactions.

concepts.name: Displacement Reaction
concepts.description: A reaction in which a more reactive chemical element displaces or expels a less reactive element from its aqueous salt solution (e.g. Iron nails dipping in copper sulphate solution).
concepts.learning_objective: Predict displacement outcomes using relative metal reactivities.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: In this reaction, iron has displaced or removed another element, copper, from copper sulphate solution. This reaction is known as displacement reaction.

concepts.name: Double Displacement Reaction
concepts.description: A chemical reaction involving mutual exchange of ions between two aqueous ionic reactant compounds to generate two new product compounds.
concepts.learning_objective: Formulate balanced double displacement equations and identify ionic exchange.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: Such reactions in which there is an exchange of ions between the reactants are called double displacement reactions.

concepts.name: Precipitation Reaction
concepts.description: A reaction resulting in the formation of an insoluble solid compound (precipitate) that settles out of an aqueous solution (e.g. BaSO4 formation from Na2SO4 and BaCl2).
concepts.learning_objective: Identify precipitates and write ionic net precipitation equations.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: Any reaction that produces a precipitate can be called a precipitation reaction. The white precipitate of BaSO4 is formed by the reaction of SO4(2-) and Ba(2+).

concepts.name: Oxidation
concepts.description: A chemical process characterized by the gain of oxygen atoms or loss of hydrogen atoms by a substance during a reaction.
concepts.learning_objective: Identify oxidized species in classical oxygen/hydrogen transfer reactions.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: If a substance gains oxygen during a reaction, it is said to be oxidised.

concepts.name: Reduction
concepts.description: A chemical process characterized by the loss of oxygen atoms or gain of hydrogen atoms by a substance during a reaction.
concepts.learning_objective: Identify reduced species in classical oxygen/hydrogen transfer reactions.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: If a substance loses oxygen during a reaction, it is said to be reduced.

concepts.name: Redox Reaction (Oxidation-Reduction Reaction)
concepts.description: A reaction occurring with concurrent and complementary oxidation and reduction, where one reactant is oxidized while another is reduced (e.g. CuO + H2 -> Cu + H2O).
concepts.learning_objective: Analyze redox reactions to identify substances oxidized, reduced, oxidizing agents, and reducing agents.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: One reactant gets oxidised while the other gets reduced during a reaction. Such reactions are called oxidation-reduction reactions or redox reactions.

concepts.name: Oxidizing and Reducing Agents
concepts.description: An oxidizing agent is a substance that causes oxidation by providing oxygen or accepting electrons (and is itself reduced); a reducing agent provides hydrogen or donates electrons (and is itself oxidized).
concepts.learning_objective: Determine the oxidizing agent and reducing agent in a redox reaction.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: In equation (1.31), carbon is oxidised to CO and ZnO is reduced to Zn... MnO2 + 4HCl -> MnCl2 + 2H2O + Cl2

concepts.name: Corrosion
concepts.description: The slow destructive chemical or electrochemical deterioration of refined metals by airborne atmospheric agents like moisture, oxygen, and carbon dioxide (e.g. Rusting of iron, black silver sulphide, green copper carbonate).
concepts.learning_objective: Describe everyday metal corrosion phenomena and identify the environmental reactants involved.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: When a metal is attacked by substances around it such as moisture, acids, etc., it is said to corrode and this process is called corrosion.

concepts.name: Rancidity
concepts.description: The aerial oxidation of unsaturated fats and oils in food substances, generating volatile degradation products causing unpleasant smell, stale taste, and nutritional decline.
concepts.learning_objective: Explain the causes of rancidity in lipid-containing foods.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: When fats and oils are oxidised, they become rancid and their smell and taste change.

concepts.name: Prevention of Oxidation in Everyday Life
concepts.description: Technological interventions to mitigate destructive oxidation: addition of antioxidants, packaging in inert gas (e.g. Nitrogen flushed chips bags), airtight refrigeration, and surface barrier coatings.
concepts.learning_objective: Evaluate prevention methods for food spoilage and metal degradation.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: Usually substances which prevent oxidation (antioxidants) are added to foods containing fats and oil... flush bags of chips with gas such as nitrogen to prevent the chips from getting oxidised.

concepts.name: Early Attempts at Classification of Elements
concepts.description: Historical grouping of chemical elements based on atomic mass and triad properties: Döbereiner's Triads and Newlands' Law of Octaves (Formative assessment only).
concepts.learning_objective: Appreciate historical developments in chemical element classification.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: Periodic classification of elements: Dobereiner's Triads, Newlands' Law of Octaves. For internal assessment only.

concepts.name: Mendeléev's Periodic Table and Modern Trends
concepts.description: Organization of elements by atomic number; modern periodic trends including valency, atomic size, metallic and non-metallic character across periods and down groups (Formative learning).
concepts.learning_objective: Trace trends in atomic radius, valency, and metallic character across the modern periodic table.

provenance_records.verbatim_text: Modern periodic table, gradation in properties, valency, atomic number, metallic and non-metallic properties.
